A trade executed late in the day near the 4:00 p.m. market close

Credit the account and permit withdrawal by wire the same day

On expiration for every out-of-the-money option held in the customer account

prompt: During new-account intake, an applicant will not give a date of birth or a taxpayer identification number. How should operations treat the application?

options.text: Do not open the account until those identity items are collected
Open the account now and limit it to sell orders until the next annual know-your-customer refresh
Open the account, because a cash account is outside the customer identification program
Open the account using the representative's own identification in place of the applicant's

explanation: The customer identification program requires the customer's name, date of birth, address, and an identification number before the firm opens the account. A later trading restriction or the representative's documents do not substitute for the missing identity data.

distractorExplanations.b: A sell-only restriction is a control on an account that already exists; it does not cure a customer identification file that was never completed.
distractorExplanations.c: The identification program applies when a cash account is opened just as it does for a margin account; the account type does not waive it.
distractorExplanations.d: The representative's identification shows who the salesperson is, not who the customer is, so it cannot complete the applicant's identification file.

prompt: Shares sit at a mutual fund company that is not a broker-dealer and cannot participate in ACATS. The customer wants them moved in. Which path should operations open?

options.text: Enter a full ACATS and expect that fund company to validate the request on the one-business-day clock
Use the fund company's own non-ACATS transfer form to move the shares
Journal the shares on the firm's books and tell the customer the outside fund cannot be moved
Submit a residual-credit request so the clearing corporation will pull the fund shares in automatically

explanation: ACATS moves accounts between broker-dealers that participate in the service. A fund company that is not a participant cannot validate that request, so operations uses the fund company's own transfer paperwork instead.

distractorExplanations.a: The one-business-day validation clock applies to a delivering broker-dealer; a fund company outside ACATS cannot validate or settle that request.
distractorExplanations.c: An internal journal moves positions the firm already carries; it cannot collect shares that are still registered at the outside fund company.
distractorExplanations.d: A residual credit forwards assets left behind after an ACATS transfer; it does not start a transfer from a firm that is not on ACATS.

prompt: An unsigned certificate, registered only in the customer's name, arrives in the mail for deposit. What must operations obtain before the transfer agent will accept it?

options.text: A notarized copy of the original purchase confirmation, which the transfer agent accepts in place of an assignment
A letter telling the transfer agent to treat the paper certificate as a book-entry position already on deposit
An endorsement or a stock power with a medallion signature guarantee
A Form 144 prepared by operations so the transfer agent can deposit the shares as restricted stock

explanation: A physical certificate is good delivery only when the registered owner assigns it, either by endorsing the certificate or by signing a separate stock power, and the signature carries a medallion guarantee the transfer agent will accept. An unsigned certificate has no assignment.

distractorExplanations.a: A purchase confirmation records a trade; it does not assign the certificate or replace the endorsement and medallion the transfer agent requires.
distractorExplanations.b: Labeling a paper certificate as book-entry does not deposit it; the transfer agent must re-register the shares after a proper assignment.
distractorExplanations.d: Form 144 is a notice for certain affiliate sales; the missing piece here is the assignment and medallion, not a sale notice.

prompt: Tonight's break shows fully paid customer shares sitting in the firm's proprietary account. What does possession-and-control procedure require operations to do?

options.text: Leave the shares there, because completing the nightly break count satisfies possession and control
Lend the shares overnight so the stock-loan record stands in for segregation and clears the break
Keep the fully paid shares available for firm use and segregate only shares that secure a customer debit
Move the fully paid shares into a possession or control location

explanation: Fully paid customer securities must be kept in the firm's possession or control and may not sit in the proprietary account. The break identifies the deficit; operations clears it by moving the shares to a permitted control location.

distractorExplanations.a: The nightly count finds the break; it does not put the shares in a control location, so the possession deficit remains.
distractorExplanations.b: Lending fully paid shares the customer has not agreed to lend removes them further from possession; a loan record is not segregation.
distractorExplanations.c: Fully paid shares are not available for firm use; shares that secure a debit are the ones that can be used, and the fully paid shares still have to be protected.

prompt: A customer's purchase has been a fail to receive for more than 30 calendar days, and the shares are still not at DTC. What should operations do?

options.text: Buy in the aged fail so the firm obtains possession of the shares
Cancel the purchase and reopen it as a when-issued trade dated today
Keep the customer marked long and leave the fail open until the contrabroker delivers on its own schedule
Park the fail in the error account and mark the customer flat

explanation: A fail to receive older than 30 calendar days that belongs to a customer long is not possession or control. Operations buys in the open fail so the firm actually obtains the shares instead of carrying the deficit.

distractorExplanations.b: Canceling the purchase and reopening it when-issued rewrites a trade that already happened; the problem is the contrabroker's failure to deliver.
distractorExplanations.c: A customer can look long on the books while the street has not delivered; after 30 calendar days that fail must be bought in, not left open.
distractorExplanations.d: The error account is for the firm's own trading mistakes; parking the fail there still leaves the customer without the securities.

prompt: Two hundred shares were posted to a customer who never entered the order, while the customer who did enter it remains flat. How should operations correct the booking?

options.text: Leave the shares with the customer who was billed and edit that customer's cost basis
Cancel that booking and rebill the trade as-of to the customer who entered the order
Sell the shares from the wrong account and send the proceeds to the customer who ordered them
Move the shares to suspense until both customers sign new account forms

explanation: A trade posted to the wrong customer is corrected by cancel and rebill as of the original trade date, so the customer who ordered the shares receives that execution. The customer who never ordered the trade should not keep the position.

distractorExplanations.a: Leaving the shares in the wrong account gives a position to someone who did not order it and leaves the real customer unfilled.
distractorExplanations.c: Selling the shares out of the wrong account replaces the original execution with a new trade and can hand the wrong customer a gain or loss that belongs in the error process.
distractorExplanations.d: Suspense is for items that cannot yet be identified; both accounts already exist, so the correction is a cancel and rebill, not a new account opening.

prompt: Free credit cash is still uninvested tonight even though the account agreement names a specific money market fund as the sweep. What should operations run?

options.text: Sweep the cash into the firm's own money market account so the balance earns the firm's overnight rate
Leave the free credit idle, because a sweep election becomes optional after the account is open
Sweep the balance into the money market fund the customer elected
Move the cash to the default bank deposit program even though the customer elected a fund

explanation: A sweep follows the standing instruction in the account agreement. Operations should invest this free credit in the elected money market fund rather than leaving it idle, substituting a bank program, or placing it in a firm account.

distractorExplanations.a: Sweeping into a firm account uses the customer's free credit for the firm; the cash has to follow the customer's election.
distractorExplanations.b: Once the agreement names a sweep fund, running that instruction is part of cashiering; treating it as optional leaves the election undone.
distractorExplanations.d: A bank deposit program is a different product from the elected money market fund; operations cannot substitute the firm's default.

prompt: The transfer agent returns a deposit because the assignment shows a notary stamp and no medallion. What should operations ask the customer to provide?

options.text: A second notary acknowledgment on the same assignment, which upgrades the first stamp
A letter signed by the representative and offered in place of a signature guarantee
A photocopy of the customer's passport so the transfer agent can waive the guarantee
A medallion signature guarantee from an eligible guarantor of the signature

explanation: Transfer agents require a medallion signature guarantee, which warrants that the signature is genuine and that the signer is the right person. A notary stamp, a representative's letter, or a passport copy does not provide that warranty.

distractorExplanations.a: A notary acknowledgment only says a signature was made; a second acknowledgment is still not a medallion guarantee.
distractorExplanations.b: The representative's letter does not warrant the signature to the transfer agent; only an eligible medallion guarantor takes on that liability.
distractorExplanations.c: A passport copy can support the firm's identity file; it does not replace the medallion the transfer agent already rejected.

prompt: A customer tenders a check payable to his brother, endorsed over to the customer, and asks that it be credited to his brokerage account. What should operations do?

options.text: Refuse the endorsed third-party check under the firm's cashiering policy
Deposit it, because the brother's endorsement makes the check payable to the customer
Deposit it into the firm's operating account and journal a credit to the customer after the check clears
Deposit it to the brother's account even though the brother is not a customer of the firm

explanation: A check payable to someone else and endorsed over is a third-party check. Brokerage cashiering policy refuses those items, because the endorsement does not make them an acceptable deposit to the customer's account.

distractorExplanations.b: An endorsement over does not turn a third-party check into a first-party deposit; the original payee is still the brother.
distractorExplanations.c: Running the check through the operating account commingles a customer item with firm funds and hides a check the cashier should have refused.
distractorExplanations.d: The brother has no account to credit; opening activity for a non-customer is not a way around a refused third-party check.

prompt: Stock loan wants to borrow fully paid shares from a cash account whose owner has never signed a securities-lending agreement. How should operations respond?

options.text: Lend the shares, because the cash-account agreement already contains general hypothecation language
Refuse the loan until the customer signs a fully paid lending agreement
Move the shares into a margin account overnight, lend them, and move them back before the next open
Lend the shares now and mail a negative-consent notice after the loan has settled

explanation: Fully paid shares in a cash account may be lent only after the customer has signed an agreement for that lending program. Operations should refuse the borrow until the agreement is on file.

distractorExplanations.a: A cash account has no margin hypothecation consent, and that kind of clause would still not authorize a loan of fully paid shares.
distractorExplanations.c: Reclassifying the account overnight to create a borrow misstates the books; the shares are fully paid and the customer gave no lending consent.
distractorExplanations.d: Notice after the loan settles lends the shares first and asks later; the written agreement has to be in place before the borrow.

prompt: Today's activity includes an equity purchase and a wire sent to a customer, and neither event is on a blotter yet. When must operations write those records?

options.text: On the monthly account statement, which replaces the daily blotter for both securities and cash
On the trade blotter for the purchase only, because the bank statement is the record of the wire
On the securities blotter and the cash blotter no later than the next business day
On next quarter's general-ledger recap, with both items added to the blotter when the annual review begins

explanation: The blotter is the daily record of purchases and sales, securities movements, and cash coming in and going out. Both the purchase and the wire belong on that record, which is prepared no later than the next business day.

distractorExplanations.a: The monthly statement reports activity to the customer; it does not replace the daily blotter of securities movements and cash.
distractorExplanations.b: The cash blotter has to itemize disbursements such as wires; a bank statement is an outside record, not the firm's blotter entry.
distractorExplanations.d: A quarterly ledger recap is too late; the blotter is written currently and is not held for an annual review.

prompt: A customer sale that executed on Tuesday was never booked, and it is now Thursday. How should operations enter the missing execution?

options.text: As a new sale dated Thursday, starting a fresh settlement cycle instead of Tuesday's contract
As a Thursday sale in the error account, with the customer told the Tuesday order expired
As a cancellation of a purchase the customer never placed, used to flatten the long position
As an as-of sale carrying Tuesday's trade date, the day the order executed

explanation: An omitted execution is posted as of the original trade date so the customer's position, proceeds, and settlement match the sale that occurred. Dating the entry Thursday creates a different trade and the wrong settlement date.

distractorExplanations.a: A Thursday sale is a new contract with a new settlement date; the customer already sold on Tuesday and is entitled to that trade.
distractorExplanations.b: The error account absorbs a firm mistake around a real customer trade; it is not a place to expire an order that did execute.
distractorExplanations.c: Canceling a purchase the customer never placed invents a trade; the missing entry is the Tuesday sale and should be added as-of.

prompt: The joint application on the desk elects rights of survivorship, but the clerk has coded tenants in common. What should operations change?

options.text: Code joint tenants with rights of survivorship, as the application states
Leave tenants in common, because every joint brokerage account is presumed to be equal shares with no survivorship
Open two individual accounts and journal half of the first deposit into each one
Code community property, treating the survivorship election as that same form of title

explanation: Operations titles the account from the agreement the customers signed. Rights of survivorship and tenants in common pass the account differently at death, so the code has to match the election on the application.

distractorExplanations.b: There is no presumption that overrides the application; tenants in common have no survivorship, and the customers selected survivorship.
distractorExplanations.c: Splitting the relationship into individual accounts discards the joint title the customers applied for and needs its own agreements.
distractorExplanations.d: Community property is a different title, used for spouses under state law; a survivorship election on a joint form is not that title.

prompt: An ACATS request is valid except for one proprietary mutual fund the receiving firm is not able to hold. How should operations treat that fund?

options.text: Force the fund through ACATS so the delivering firm must liquidate it during validation
Except the fund from the transfer and have the customer sell it or leave it behind
Reject the entire transfer, because one asset the receiver cannot hold voids every other position
Book the fund in the error account and credit the customer cash equal to the prior net asset value

explanation: ACATS can move only assets the receiving firm can carry. A proprietary fund the receiver cannot hold is excepted from the transfer, and the customer sells it or leaves it at the delivering firm while the other assets proceed.

distractorExplanations.a: The delivering firm does not have to liquidate an asset during validation just because the receiver cannot hold it; forcing the fund through ACATS is not a valid instruction.
distractorExplanations.c: One ineligible position does not cancel assets that can move; operations excepts the fund and continues the rest of the transfer.
distractorExplanations.d: The error account is for firm trade breaks, not for housing a customer's mutual fund, and a net-asset-value credit is not a transfer.

prompt: The contrabroker presents a certificate registered to someone else, with the quantity line torn through. Why is that tender not good delivery?

options.text: Because every physical certificate is bad delivery now that equities move only by book-entry at the depository
Because the trade date is more than one business day old, so physical delivery has become optional
Because the certificate is not in negotiable form and is not in the right name
Because a delivery must be rejected whenever the original trade confirmation is not attached to the certificate

explanation: Good delivery of a paper certificate requires a negotiable instrument in the right name or properly assigned. A certificate registered to someone else and torn through the quantity fails both conditions, so operations rejects the tender.

distractorExplanations.a: An intact, properly assigned certificate can still be good delivery; the defects here are the wrong registration and the torn quantity line.
distractorExplanations.b: The age of the trade does not make a mutilated, wrongly registered certificate acceptable; settlement still requires good delivery.
distractorExplanations.d: The trade confirmation does not cure title or condition; the rejection is based on the torn certificate and the wrong registered owner.

prompt: The customer ledger is long fully paid shares, but those shares are an open fail to receive and are not in any depository. How should operations classify them?

options.text: In control, because the customer account already shows a long position
In possession, because an open fail to receive counts as a control location for the reserve
In transfer, which counts as possession for as long as the fail remains open
Not in possession or control while those shares remain an open fail to receive

explanation: A fail to receive is a claim on the street, not a control location. Fully paid customer shares count as in possession or control only when the firm holds them or has them at a permitted location such as a depository.

distractorExplanations.a: The customer ledger can show a long position the street has not delivered; that book entry does not place the shares in possession or control.
distractorExplanations.b: A fail to receive is the opposite of a control location; the reserve computation does not convert an undelivered fail into possession.
distractorExplanations.c: Securities in transfer are certificates at a transfer agent, not an open street fail; an open fail is not possession.

prompt: After an equity fail to deliver, the buying firm serves a buy-in notice. What outcome should the selling firm's operations staff expect?

options.text: The buyer may purchase the shares in and charge the failing seller
The notice is a sell-out, so the seller must wire cash instead of delivering shares
The fail is cancelled if the seller compares the trade as a DK before the next opening
The buyer must wait until both firms agree on a new settlement date before the fail can be closed

explanation: A buy-in closes a seller's fail to deliver. After the required notice, the buyer can purchase the shares in the market and charge the cost to the firm that failed to deliver. A sell-out is the different remedy used when a buyer fails to pay.

distractorExplanations.b: A sell-out closes a buyer's failure to pay for securities; this notice is a buy-in of the seller's failure to deliver shares.
distractorExplanations.c: A DK questions whether a trade exists; it does not erase a buy-in notice on a fail the seller already owes.
distractorExplanations.d: A buy-in lets the buyer close the fail without waiting for a voluntary new settlement date once notice procedures are met.

prompt: The execution report shows the customer's limit was filled, but the account was booked at a worse price. What should operations correct?

options.text: Leave the worse price on the customer and book the difference as commission revenue
Give the customer the reported price and book the difference to the error account
Cancel the fill and ask the customer to enter a new order at the worse price
Average the reported price and the booked price on the confirmation so the customer and the firm split the difference

explanation: The customer is entitled to the price on the execution report. Operations corrects the account to that price and records the firm's loss in the error account, where a principal can review the mistake.

distractorExplanations.a: The difference is a firm error, not a commission; leaving the worse price on the customer keeps the benefit of the mistake at the firm.
distractorExplanations.c: The order already filled at the better price; canceling it and asking for a new order takes that fill away from the customer.
distractorExplanations.d: Splitting the difference still denies the customer part of the reported execution; the error account, not the customer, absorbs the firm's mistake.

prompt: Cleared check proceeds are a free credit, and the new account file contains no sweep election. Where should operations leave that cash?

options.text: In the firm's preferred bank sweep, treating the account opening as consent to that program
In a money market fund, so the customer is invested while the sweep paperwork is still pending
As a free credit balance in the account until the customer elects a sweep
In the firm's operating account, with interest paid only if the customer later complains

explanation: With no sweep election on file, customer cash remains a free credit balance the firm must be prepared to pay on demand. Operations should not choose a bank program or a fund for the customer, and should not move the cash into the operating account.

distractorExplanations.a: Negative consent to a sweep requires the firm's disclosed program and the required notice; opening the account does not silently elect a bank.
distractorExplanations.b: Buying a money market fund is an investment the customer has not authorized; unfinished paperwork is not an election.
distractorExplanations.d: Free credits are customer funds; moving them into the operating account commingles them with firm money.

prompt: A customer who signed a certificate at home asks the cashier to medallion-guarantee the signature. The customer is not present and identity has not been checked. What should operations do?

options.text: Apply the medallion because the signature resembles the driver's-license image already stored in the account file
Apply the medallion and note that the registered representative says the customer is known to the desk
Stamp a firm notary seal on the assignment, which transfer agents accept as a medallion guarantee
Decline the guarantee until the signer is identified under the medallion program

explanation: A medallion guarantee warrants the signature, so the guarantor has to identify the signer under the program's rules before stamping. A file image, a representative's assurance, or a notary seal is not that identification.

distractorExplanations.a: A license image already in the file does not prove who signed the certificate at home; guaranteeing that signature makes the firm the warrantor.
distractorExplanations.b: A representative's statement that the customer is known does not complete the program's identification of the person who signed.
distractorExplanations.c: A notary seal is not a medallion, and transfer agents reject it; operations should not relabel a notary stamp as a guarantee.

prompt: A check made payable to the broker-dealer, for the benefit of a named customer and showing that account number, arrives in the mail. What should operations do with it?

options.text: Credit the named customer and process the check as a customer deposit
Deposit the check into firm revenue because the broker-dealer, not the customer, is the payee named on the face
Return the check as a third-party item because the customer is not the payee printed on the face
Hold the check unapplied in the vault until the customer signs a deposit slip in a branch

explanation: A check payable to the firm for the benefit of a named customer is that customer's deposit. Operations credits the account on the check and handles the item as customer funds, not as firm revenue and not as an unidentified hold.

distractorExplanations.b: The firm is the payee as nominee for the customer identified on the check; crediting revenue would take the customer's money.
distractorExplanations.c: For-the-benefit-of language with an account number makes this a customer deposit, not a third-party check payable to an outside person.
distractorExplanations.d: The check already identifies the account; waiting for a branch deposit slip leaves a known customer deposit unapplied.

prompt: The lender recalls stock the firm borrowed to support a customer short, and the recall date arrives before the customer covers. What should operations do?

options.text: Keep the borrowed shares until the customer buys to cover, and use that purchase as the return
Return the borrowed shares, or replace the borrow, in time to meet the lender's recall
Move the borrowed shares into the error account and mark the customer short as flat
Buy the customer in the same day and charge that purchase to the lender who issued the recall

explanation: A recall requires the borrowing firm to give the shares back. Operations returns them from a new borrow or from other available shares in time for the recall, rather than keeping the lender's stock until the customer chooses to cover.

distractorExplanations.a: The customer's covering timetable does not postpone a lender's recall; the firm borrowed the shares and has to return them when called.
distractorExplanations.c: The error account does not close a stock loan, and marking the short flat would misstate a position that is still open.
distractorExplanations.d: Charging a buy-in to the lender reverses the parties; the lender is calling its shares back, not paying for a close-out of the customer's short.

prompt: Couriers drop off stock certificates the same afternoon a cashier wires funds out to a customer. Which blotter entries does operations owe?

options.text: A single trade-blotter line for both events, because the monthly statement is the record of receipts and wires
A securities-blotter entry only, because the bank reconciliation already captures every outgoing wire
A securities receipt on the securities blotter and the wire on the cash blotter
No blotter entry until both items have been reviewed in the annual count of the vault and the bank

explanation: The securities blotter records certificates coming in and going out, and the cash blotter records cash coming in and going out. A certificate receipt and a wire are separate events, and each needs its own current blotter line.

distractorExplanations.a: The customer statement is not the blotter, and one trade line does not record a certificate receipt or a cash wire.
distractorExplanations.b: The bank reconciliation supports the cash books, but the firm still itemizes the wire on its cash blotter, and that reconciliation does not record the certificates.
distractorExplanations.d: Blotters are daily records prepared currently; they are not written for the first time at an annual count.

prompt: An as-of purchase carries a trade date before the ex-dividend date, but it was booked only after the record date, and the dividend did not post. What should operations do?

options.text: Drop the dividend, because an as-of trade loses the dividend once the record date has passed
Credit a goodwill dividend from the error account without checking which account was the holder of record
Change the trade date to the record date so the customer looks long for the dividend without a claim
Claim the dividend from the delivering side based on the original trade date

explanation: An as-of entry keeps the original trade date. A purchase dated before the ex-dividend date is entitled to that dividend, so operations claims it from the side that was paid instead of rewriting the trade date or booking a goodwill credit.

distractorExplanations.a: Passing the record date on the booking calendar does not erase entitlement; the as-of trade date, before the ex-dividend date, is what decides who is owed the dividend.
distractorExplanations.b: A goodwill credit spends firm money on a street claim; operations should claim the dividend from the party who received it.
distractorExplanations.c: Moving the trade date onto the record date rewrites the contract and can change settlement; the original trade date already supports the claim.

prompt: A lawyer offers her own driver's license and a corporate resolution to open a company account. What additional identity work should operations finish first?

options.text: Identify the beneficial owners of the company and one person who controls the entity
Accept the lawyer's own license, treating the person who signed the resolution as the customer
Collect a Form U4 for every director so the company can be approved as an associated person of the firm
Obtain a medallion guarantee of the resolution, which replaces beneficial-owner identification

explanation: Opening a legal-entity account requires identification of the beneficial owners and of one individual who controls the company, followed by verification of those people. The signer's license shows who presented the resolution; it does not identify who owns or controls the entity.

distractorExplanations.b: The lawyer is an agent who signed the resolution; identification and beneficial-owner diligence look through to the company's owners and a control person.
distractorExplanations.c: Form U4 registers associated persons of a broker-dealer; directors of a customer company are not registered that way in order to open the account.
distractorExplanations.d: A medallion guarantee warrants a signature on a securities transfer; it does not identify beneficial owners or satisfy entity due diligence.

prompt: An IRA owner wants the assets moved from a bank trustee that is not an ACATS participant, without taking a distribution. Which process should operations use?

options.text: A full ACATS request, because every retirement account is required to move through the clearing corporation
A non-ACATS trustee-to-trustee transfer arranged directly with the bank
A rollover check made payable to the customer, for the customer to deposit back into an IRA
A residual-credit sweep after an ACATS submission the bank is required to accept

explanation: A bank trustee that does not participate in ACATS cannot validate a clearing-corporation transfer. Operations arranges a non-ACATS trustee-to-trustee movement so the assets go between custodians and the customer does not take a distribution.

distractorExplanations.a: ACATS is for participating broker-dealers; a bank trustee outside the service will not validate that request.
distractorExplanations.c: A check payable to the customer is a distribution, which is the outcome the customer asked to avoid, not a trustee-to-trustee transfer.
distractorExplanations.d: A residual credit follows an ACATS that already moved; it cannot force a non-participant bank to accept ACATS.

prompt: Settlement staff propose to deliver an institutional DVP sale to the custodian today and collect the cash next week. What should operations require instead?

options.text: Free-deliver the shares today, because the institution is an established client and the custodian will pay next week
Deliver the shares into the firm's error account and hold them there until the custodian wires payment
Release the securities to the custodian only against simultaneous payment
Cancel the institutional trade and rebook it as a purchase in the salesperson's individual cash account

explanation: Delivery versus payment means the securities move only against payment. Free-delivering to the custodian before the cash arrives gives away the shares and creates the collection risk the DVP instruction was meant to prevent.

distractorExplanations.a: Knowing the institution does not change a DVP instruction into a free delivery; the shares stay until payment is made.
distractorExplanations.b: The error account is not a warehouse for a customer's DVP trade; parking the shares there misstates both the customer and the firm.
distractorExplanations.d: The institutional trade is valid; moving it into the salesperson's account is an unauthorized rebilling, not a way to settle DVP.

prompt: A bank loan is secured in part by a customer's fully paid shares that were swept in with the margin collateral. What should operations correct?

options.text: Nothing, because every position carried in a margin account may be pledged to the firm's bank loan
The label on the loan, calling it nonpurpose, which allows the fully paid shares to remain pledged
Pledge an equal quantity of proprietary shares and leave the customer's fully paid shares at the bank
Release the fully paid shares from the bank loan and return them to possession or control

explanation: Fully paid customer securities have to stay in the firm's possession or control and cannot be left in a bank pledge. Operations releases those shares from the loan and returns them to a control location.

distractorExplanations.a: A margin account can still hold fully paid securities, and those shares are not collateral the firm may pledge to its bank.
distractorExplanations.b: Renaming the loan nonpurpose does not change the rule; fully paid customer shares are not pledgeable collateral.
distractorExplanations.c: Adding proprietary shares at the bank while the customer's fully paid shares stay pledged does not return those customer shares to possession or control.

prompt: Certificates from a customer long sale are still at the transfer agent, the firm is failing to deliver, and the buyer has warned of a buy-in. What should operations do?

options.text: Get the certificates through transfer quickly, or buy shares in before the close-out
Cancel the customer's long sale and explain that a transfer-agent delay voids the execution
DK the original sale so the buyer's buy-in notice no longer applies
Shift the fail into suspense and answer that a buy-in is the remedy for a short sale

explanation: The customer's long sale remains a valid trade. If certificates in transfer leave the firm unable to deliver, operations gets them back quickly or buys shares in before the buy-in, and does not cancel or DK the execution.

distractorExplanations.b: A delay at the transfer agent is the firm's delivery problem; it does not void a sale the customer already made from a long position.
distractorExplanations.c: A DK is for a trade the firm does not recognize; using it to dodge a buy-in misstates a sale that is on the books.
distractorExplanations.d: A buy-in closes a fail to deliver whether the original sale was long or short; suspense does not stop the buyer's close-out.

prompt: A regular-way corporate bond trade is executed on Tuesday in a week with no market holiday. When should operations expect that trade to settle?

options.text: Tuesday, because corporate debt settles the same day even though equities settle one business day later
Thursday, on the retired two-business-day cycle, which still applies to corporate debt after equities moved
Wednesday, because most corporate-debt trades settle one business day later
The following Monday, because corporate-bond settlement waits for the next interest payment date

explanation: Most corporate-debt trades settle T+1, one business day after the trade date, the same standard cycle as equities. A Tuesday regular-way corporate bond trade in a normal week therefore settles on Wednesday.

distractorExplanations.a: Same-day settlement is a special cash trade; regular-way corporate debt does not settle on the trade date.
distractorExplanations.b: Corporate debt moved to T+1 with equities; settling the bond two business days later would fail the trade.
distractorExplanations.d: Interest payment dates govern the coupon, not the settlement cycle; regular-way settlement does not wait for the next interest date.

Copies of all customer complaints and their resolution for four years
Fingerprint records and Form U4 filings for associated persons
Customer account information including identity and contact details

explanation: 4512 governs customer account recordkeeping content and updates.

distractorExplanations.a: Written supervisory procedures are required by FINRA Rule 3110, not by Rule 4512's customer account information rule.
distractorExplanations.b: Customer complaint records are FINRA Rule 4513 (four years); Rule 4512 covers account information such as name, residence, and trusted contact.

explanation: FINRA allows 90 minutes for the Series 99. That clock covers the full form, both the 50 scored questions and the 5 unscored pretest questions. The appointment is not extended for pretest items, and it is not the longer SIE or Series 7 top-off session.

distractorExplanations.a: Confuses the Series 99 appointment with the SIE. The SIE session is longer; the Series 99 appointment is 90 minutes.
distractorExplanations.c: Limits the clock to the scored section. The 90 minutes covers every question on the form, including pretest items.
distractorExplanations.d: Confuses the Series 99 with the Series 7 top-off, which uses a much longer appointment. Series 99 is 90 minutes.

prompt: Which description of the Series 99 passing score is right?

options.text: 34 correct answers out of the 50 scored items, on every form
68 percent of all 55 questions, with pretest items included in the percentage
An equated score of 68, so the raw number correct can differ by form
A cut score each sponsoring firm sets after the sitting and reports in place of a published passing score

explanation: FINRA's passing score for the Series 99 is 68 on an equated scale. Equating means the raw number of scored items that must be correct can differ by form, so 68 is not a promise that 34 out of 50 always passes, and it is not 68 percent of the 55 questions on the screen. The sponsoring firm does not set the cut score.

distractorExplanations.a: Treats 68 as a raw 34 out of 50. Because the score is equated, the raw number required can change from form to form.
distractorExplanations.b: Turns 68 into a percentage of all 55 questions and counts pretest items. The passing score is an equated 68 based on the scored items.
distractorExplanations.d: Gives the cut score to the sponsoring firm. The passing score is FINRA's equated 68.

prompt: Which fee does FINRA charge a candidate to take the Series 99?

options.text: No published FINRA fee, because the sponsoring firm's registration charge already includes this exam and the SIE
No separate fee once the candidate has paid to sit for the SIE
No fee when the firm, rather than the candidate, requests the exam window
FINRA charges an examination fee of $100, and sponsorship does not replace that fee

explanation: FINRA's fee for the Series 99 examination is $100. Sponsorship is a separate requirement: the member firm must open the window, and that sponsorship does not erase the fee. Paying for the SIE, or having the firm request the window, does not waive the Series 99 fee either.

distractorExplanations.a: Confuses sponsorship with a fee waiver. The firm must sponsor the candidate, and FINRA still charges $100 for the Series 99.
distractorExplanations.b: Treats the SIE payment as covering both exams. The SIE and the Series 99 are separate exams, and the Series 99 fee is $100.
distractorExplanations.c: Makes the fee depend on who requests the window. FINRA charges $100 for the Series 99 whether the firm or the candidate handles scheduling.

prompt: What is the SIE's role for someone who must register as an Operations Professional?

options.text: It is a corequisite: both exams are required, in either order
It is a prerequisite and must be passed before the Series 99 window can be opened
Passing the SIE alone completes Operations Professional registration, so the Series 99 top-off is optional
Back-office staff are exempt from the SIE and take the Series 99 by itself

explanation: The SIE is a corequisite of the Series 99, not a substitute for it and not an exam that must be passed first. An operations employee may take the two exams in either order, but registration as an Operations Professional waits until both have been passed and a member firm has sponsored the Series 99.

distractorExplanations.b: Misreads corequisite as prerequisite. The SIE may be taken before or after the Series 99; it does not have to come first.
distractorExplanations.c: Treats the SIE as sufficient registration. The Series 99 top-off is still required for an Operations Professional.
distractorExplanations.d: Exempts operations staff from the SIE. Both the SIE and the Series 99 are required; there is no back-office exemption from the corequisite.

prompt: May an individual enroll for the Series 99 without a FINRA member firm?

options.text: Yes. The Series 99 is open to unsponsored candidates on the same basis as the Securities Industry Essentials exam
No. A member firm must sponsor the candidate and open the window
Yes. Paying the examination fee lets the candidate self-enroll
Yes. A passed SIE authorizes the candidate to open a Series 99 window without a firm

explanation: The Series 99 requires sponsorship by a FINRA member firm. The firm requests the exam window; an individual cannot open it alone. The SIE is the exam that does not require sponsorship, and passing it does not remove the sponsorship requirement. Paying the $100 fee is not a substitute for a sponsoring firm.

distractorExplanations.a: Confuses the Series 99 with the SIE. The SIE can be taken without a firm; the Series 99 cannot.
distractorExplanations.c: Treats the fee as enrollment authority. Paying the examination fee does not open a window; a member firm must sponsor the candidate.
distractorExplanations.d: Treats a passed SIE as permission to self-enroll. The SIE is the corequisite, and the Series 99 still requires a sponsoring member.

prompt: How many scored Series 99 items address professional conduct and ethical considerations?

options.text: 15, but they sit in Function 1 with the operations-knowledge items
35, because conduct is the larger of the two functions
15 scored items, and that block is Function 2, professional conduct
All 50 scored items, because conduct is woven through every operations question instead of standing as its own function

explanation: Function 2 of the Series 99 outline is professional conduct and ethical considerations, and it accounts for 15 of the 50 scored items. The other 35 scored items are Function 1, securities industry and broker-dealer operations knowledge. Conduct is its own function, and it is not the larger of the two.

distractorExplanations.a: Assigns the 15 conduct items to Function 1. Function 1 is the 35-item operations-knowledge section; Function 2 is the 15-item conduct section.
distractorExplanations.b: Swaps the weights. Thirty-five scored items test operations knowledge; professional conduct is the 15-item function.
distractorExplanations.d: Treats conduct as the entire scored exam. Only 15 scored items are in the professional-conduct function.

prompt: A candidate fails the Series 99 once, on 2 February 2027. Which waiting period applies before the next attempt?

options.text: 30 days, the first-failure wait used before 19 January 2027
180 days, because a first failure now carries the longest qualification-exam wait
No waiting period, if the sponsoring firm reopens the window the next day
15 days, the first-failure wait that applies after 19 January 2027

explanation: Beginning 19 January 2027, FINRA's retake waits are 15 days after a first failure, 15 days after a second failure, and 60 days after a third or later failure. A single failure on 2 February 2027 therefore carries a 15-day wait. The former 30-day first-failure wait does not apply, and a firm cannot waive the wait by reopening a window.

distractorExplanations.a: States the first-failure wait that applied before 19 January 2027. After that date the first-failure wait is 15 days, not 30.
distractorExplanations.b: Applies the old third-failure wait of 180 days to a first failure. After 19 January 2027 a first failure waits 15 days.
distractorExplanations.c: Lets the sponsoring firm erase the wait. After this first failure the candidate must wait 15 days, even if the firm is ready to reopen a window.

prompt: A new-accounts specialist is coding a corporate delivery-versus-payment account. A person who is not on the authorized-trader list emails settlement instructions. What does FINRA Rule 2090 require?

options.text: Confirm who may act for the customer, and do not take the unauthorized instructions
Process the email, because identity was already checked when the account opened
Leave authority questions to sales and process any instruction that names the account
File the email as a Rule 4530 complaint and wait for FINRA to approve that sender before any settlement instruction is accepted

explanation: FINRA Rule 2090 requires reasonable diligence, when an account is opened and while it is maintained, to know the essential facts about the customer and the authority of each person acting for the customer. Settlement instructions from someone who is not authorized must not be accepted. An opening identity check does not cure a later authority problem, and the email is not a Rule 4530 complaint.

distractorExplanations.b: Confuses an opening identity check with ongoing authority. Rule 2090 still requires the firm to know who may act for the customer after the account exists.
distractorExplanations.c: Pushes know-your-customer onto sales. Operations staff who accept instructions must know the sender's authority under Rule 2090.
distractorExplanations.d: Misfiles an unauthorized instruction as a Rule 4530 complaint and invents a FINRA pre-approval step that Rule 2090 does not require.

prompt: At what point does FINRA Rule 2090 require a firm to know the essential facts about a customer whose account operations staff service?

options.text: On the day the account is opened
When the account is opened and for as long as the firm carries it
When a representative recommends a security to a retail customer
During the annual branch inspection, when a principal samples new-account forms and signs the know-your-customer file

explanation: Rule 2090 requires reasonable diligence in regard to the opening and the maintenance of every account. Essential facts are those the firm needs in order to service the account, follow special handling instructions, understand who has authority, and comply with applicable rules. The duty does not end at onboarding, and it is not limited to a retail recommendation or to the annual inspection sample.

distractorExplanations.a: Stops the duty at account opening. Rule 2090 expressly covers maintenance of the account, not just the day it is opened.
distractorExplanations.c: Confuses Rule 2090 with a retail-recommendation standard. The duty applies to accounts operations staff service even when nobody is making a recommendation.
distractorExplanations.d: Reduces an ongoing duty to an annual sample. The firm must know essential facts throughout the time it maintains the account.

prompt: A carrying firm's transfer desk is told to stall a customer's account-transfer request until a recruiting dispute with the departing representative ends. There is no lien, and the instruction is complete. Which rule does the stall violate?

options.text: No FINRA rule, because a firm may defend its recruiting pipeline
Rule 11870, and only after the stall lasts past the settlement cycle
FINRA Rule 2140, which forbids interfering with this customer transfer
Regulation Best Interest, as if the hold were a recommendation that the customer stay

explanation: FINRA Rule 2140 prohibits a member from interfering with a customer's request to transfer an account in connection with a registered representative's change of employment, unless the account is subject to a lien or another bona fide claim. A recruiting dispute is the interference the rule targets. The transfer-procedure rule does not authorize the stall, and Regulation Best Interest is not the standard for this hold.

distractorExplanations.a: Treats a recruiting dispute as a permitted business reason. Rule 2140 exists so a firm cannot hold customer accounts hostage to that dispute.
distractorExplanations.b: Misstates both the rule and the timing. Rule 2140 bars the interference itself; the firm does not get a free stall until the settlement cycle passes.
distractorExplanations.d: Names Regulation Best Interest, which governs recommendations to retail customers. This hold is interference with a transfer under Rule 2140.

prompt: A carrying firm receives a complete instruction to transfer a customer account. The account has no lien and no document defect. What does FINRA Rule 11870 require?

options.text: Wait for the representative of record to approve the move before validating the instruction
Move the securities and keep any residual cash until the customer sends a second request
Reject the instruction because the representative has resigned, and ask the customer to resubmit after a retention call
Validate the instruction and complete the transfer rather than sit on it

explanation: FINRA Rule 11870 is the customer account-transfer contract. When the instruction is complete and no valid exception applies, the carrying firm validates and completes the transfer. It may not condition validation on the representative's consent, hold residual cash back, or invent an exception because the representative has resigned.

distractorExplanations.a: Adds a representative-consent step Rule 11870 does not allow. The customer's complete instruction is what the carrying firm must act on.
distractorExplanations.b: Withholds residual cash that belongs in the transfer. The rule covers the account transfer, not a securities-only shipment with cash held behind.
distractorExplanations.c: Treats a resignation as a transfer exception. A representative's departure is not a document defect or a lien, so it is not a reason to reject a complete instruction.

prompt: Operations is asked to split one household mutual-fund purchase into two tickets so each ticket stays just below the fund's sales-charge breakpoint, and the higher load is billed on both. What is that split?

options.text: A breakpoint sale that FINRA Rule 2342 prohibits in order to stop the higher sales charge
A letter of intent, which secures the lower sales charge on a later purchase
Rights of accumulation, which require splitting the purchase so each ticket stays under the breakpoint
A best-execution method under Rule 5310, used so two smaller tickets print at a better price than one purchase at the breakpoint

explanation: FINRA Rule 2342 prohibits selling investment-company shares in an amount just below a breakpoint in order to share in the higher sales charge. Splitting one household purchase so both tickets miss the reduced load is that practice. A letter of intent and rights of accumulation help a customer reach the lower charge; they are not reasons to keep the higher load. Best execution does not authorize the split.

distractorExplanations.b: Misnames the split as a letter of intent. A letter of intent qualifies the customer for the reduced load; it is not a way to bill the higher load twice.
distractorExplanations.c: Treats rights of accumulation as a reason to split the purchase below the breakpoint. Those rights combine qualifying holdings so the customer receives the lower sales charge.
distractorExplanations.d: Invokes best execution. Rule 5310 is about the market for a customer order, not about structuring fund purchases to preserve a higher sales charge.

prompt: Trade-support staff learn that a customer block is about to reach the market and is not yet public. A firm proprietary account then buys that stock. Which prohibition does the buy violate?

options.text: Rule 5320, and the buy is a problem only if a customer limit order was already resting
FINRA Rule 5270, which bans front running a block before the block is public
No rule, when the buy is booked in an operations error account
FINRA Rule 2342, on the theory that buying ahead of a customer block is the same abuse as selling fund shares just below a breakpoint

explanation: FINRA Rule 5270 prohibits a member or associated person who has material nonpublic information about an imminent block from causing a trade in that security, or in a related instrument, before information about the block is public. Staff who saw the pending block and then bought the stock for a firm account are front running. An error-account label does not take the trade outside the rule.

distractorExplanations.a: Names Rule 5320, which concerns a customer order the firm has accepted and is holding. This buy is ahead of an imminent block and falls under Rule 5270 even with no resting limit order.
distractorExplanations.c: Assumes an error-account code is a defense. Rule 5270 still applies to a proprietary buy made with nonpublic knowledge of the block.
distractorExplanations.d: Cites the breakpoint-sales rule. Rule 2342 addresses mutual-fund sales charges, not a proprietary equity buy ahead of a block.

prompt: The firm accepts a customer's equity limit order, holds it unexecuted, and then buys that stock for a proprietary account at a price that would have filled the customer. The customer remains unfilled. Which rule is breached?

options.text: FINRA Rule 5270, the rule for trading ahead of an imminent block
No rule, because a proprietary order outranks a customer limit order
FINRA Rule 5320, because the firm traded ahead of a customer order it was holding
FINRA Rule 2140, as if skipping the customer were interference with an account transfer

explanation: FINRA Rule 5320 prohibits a member that accepts and holds a customer equity order from trading that security for its own account on the same side, at a price that would satisfy the customer, unless it immediately thereafter fills the customer at the same or better price. Leaving the customer unfilled is trading ahead. The block rule and the account-transfer rule address different conduct.

distractorExplanations.a: Confuses a held customer order with an imminent block. Rule 5270 covers nonpublic knowledge of a block; Rule 5320 covers the order the firm has accepted and is holding.
distractorExplanations.b: Reverses priority. A firm may not buy for its own account at a price that would satisfy a customer order it is holding and then leave that customer unfilled.
distractorExplanations.d: Cites the account-transfer rule. Nothing in this fact pattern is a transfer request; the breach is trading ahead under Rule 5320.

prompt: A desk inserts a second broker between a customer order and the market. The extra broker charges an added fee and does not improve the customer's price. How should FINRA Rule 5310 be applied?

options.text: Disclosure of the extra fee on the confirmation ends the firm's duty
The insertion is permitted when the second broker is an affiliate
The insertion is a breakpoint sale under Rule 2342, because adding a broker keeps a fund purchase just below a sales-charge reduction
The extra broker is improper interpositioning and the routing fails best execution

explanation: FINRA Rule 5310 requires reasonable diligence to obtain the most favorable price for the customer under prevailing market conditions. Interposing a broker that adds cost and does not improve the fill fails that duty. A confirmation disclosure does not cure the routing, an affiliate relationship is not permission, and the breakpoint-sales rule is about investment-company loads rather than an extra broker in the execution chain.

distractorExplanations.a: Treats a confirmation disclosure as a waiver of best execution. Rule 5310 still requires reasonable diligence to find the best market.
distractorExplanations.b: Assumes an affiliate may be inserted at the customer's expense. Affiliation does not excuse an intermediary that worsens the customer's price.
distractorExplanations.c: Names the breakpoint-sales rule. Rule 2342 does not govern an extra broker placed in a secondary-market execution.

prompt: An operations associate knows a customer's transfer request was never entered, yet tells the customer the request is in process at the receiving firm. Which standard does that statement fail?

options.text: Rule 2010's standards of commercial honor and just principles of trade
Rule 5310, and the statement matters only if the missed transfer would have produced a worse price
No FINRA standard, because the speaker works in operations rather than in sales
Rule 4530, but only after the customer sends a third written complaint about the same transfer status

explanation: FINRA Rule 2010 requires a member and its associated persons, in the conduct of the firm's business, to observe high standards of commercial honor and just and equitable principles of trade. An operations associate who knowingly gives a customer a false transfer status breaches that standard. The duty is not limited to salespeople, and it does not wait for a third complaint or for a worse price.

distractorExplanations.b: Substitutes best execution for a false statement. Rule 5310 is about the market for an order; the failure here is a dishonest status, which Rule 2010 covers.
distractorExplanations.c: Limits Rule 2010 to sales staff. Associated persons in operations are held to the same standards of commercial honor in the firm's business.
distractorExplanations.d: Imports a three-complaint count the rule does not use. A knowing misstatement fails Rule 2010 when it is made, not after a third letter arrives.

prompt: A supervisor directs a ledger clerk to reclassify a customer's free credit as firm cash so an aged reconciliation break disappears. The clerk knows the entry is false. What must the clerk do?

options.text: Post the entry, because a supervisor's instruction shifts responsibility off the clerk
Refuse the false entry and escalate it; the books must show the real credit
Post the entry for the report date and reverse it after any examination
Park the credit in suspense with no blotter note, as if that were outside the books duty

explanation: Broker-dealer books and records must reflect real positions and customer balances. Posting an entry the clerk knows is false, in order to hide a break, destroys that integrity whether or not a supervisor asked for it. Parking the credit in an unnoted suspense account, or reversing the lie after an examination, is the same failure. The clerk must refuse the false entry and escalate it.

distractorExplanations.a: Treats a supervisor's order as a defense to a false posting. The person who enters a known false credit still violates the duty to keep accurate books.
distractorExplanations.c: Plans to repair the lie later. A false entry is improper when it is posted; timing it around an examination does not make the record true.
distractorExplanations.d: Hides the credit off the blotter. Moving a customer free credit into an unnoted suspense account is another false record, not a permitted cleanup.

prompt: To conceal a late corporate-action instruction, an associate changes the blotter timestamp to the previous day. The share quantity and account number are correct. Why does the changed timestamp still matter?

options.text: It does not matter, because the quantity and the account number are right
Timestamps may be rewritten until the nightly ledger extract is produced
The blotter no longer truthfully records when the firm actually entered the instruction
Rule 2010 permits the new timestamp when it matches the effective date the customer requested, even though the firm entered the instruction later

explanation: A blotter is a record of what the firm did and when. Changing the timestamp to conceal a late entry makes that record false even if the quantity and account number are right. The nightly extract is not a window for rewriting history, and commercial honor does not authorize a backdated entry that hides when the firm actually acted. A real correction is a new entry, not a rewritten time.

distractorExplanations.a: Treats two accurate fields as a cure for a false one. A record that misstates when the firm acted is still not a true book.
distractorExplanations.b: Invents a rewrite window before the nightly extract. The timestamp has to record the real time of the entry, not a time chosen before a batch job.
distractorExplanations.d: Misuses Rule 2010. Matching a date the customer requested does not justify altering the record of when the firm actually entered the instruction.

prompt: Under FINRA Rule 2140, which fact allows a carrying firm to decline a customer's request to transfer an account with a departing representative?

options.text: The representative has refused to consent to the transfer
The receiving firm is the competitor that just hired the representative
The customer has not attended a retention meeting at which the carrying firm can argue that the customer should stay
The account is subject to a lien for money the customer owes the firm

explanation: Rule 2140 bars interference with a customer transfer tied to a representative's change of employment, except where the account is subject to a lien for money the customer owes or another bona fide claim. Lack of the representative's consent, the identity of the receiving firm, and a demand for a retention meeting are the interference the rule prohibits, not reasons to decline the transfer.

distractorExplanations.a: Treats the representative's refusal as a veto. Rule 2140 stops the firm from conditioning the customer's transfer on that consent.
distractorExplanations.b: Treats a competitor's hire as an exception. That employment change is why the transfer must proceed, absent a lien or other bona fide claim.
distractorExplanations.c: Adds a retention meeting the rule does not require. Holding the account until the customer attends one is interference under Rule 2140.

prompt: Which considerations does FINRA Rule 5310 tell a desk to weigh when judging reasonable diligence to obtain the best market?

options.text: Market character, order size and type, markets checked, quotation access, and the order's terms
Which venue paid the firm the highest rebate on that order
Whether the customer later complained in writing about the fill
Whether the order was a mutual-fund purchase sized just below a breakpoint, which this rule uses in place of the market factors

explanation: FINRA Rule 5310 lists the factors for reasonable diligence: the character of the market for the security, the size and type of transaction, the number of markets checked, the accessibility of the quotation, and the terms and conditions of the order. A rebate, a later complaint, and a mutual-fund breakpoint do not replace that review. Breakpoint sales are a separate rule.

distractorExplanations.b: Reduces best execution to the highest rebate. Rule 5310 requires a review of the market factors it lists, and a rebate does not by itself pick the market.
distractorExplanations.c: Makes the duty complaint-driven. Reasonable diligence is required when the firm handles the order, not only after a customer writes in.
distractorExplanations.d: Imports the breakpoint-sales test. Rule 5310's factors are market factors for the customer order, not a fund's sales-charge schedule.

prompt: A firm buys for its own account at a price that would fill a customer equity order it is holding. It executes the customer order at that price the next morning. Does FINRA Rule 5320 permit the overnight gap?

options.text: Yes. Filling the customer at the same price the next business day cures the proprietary trade
No. The customer execution must follow at once, at that price or better
Yes. Proprietary equity accounts are exempt from the trading-ahead rule
No, unless the held order was a block, in which case only the front-running rule applies

explanation: Rule 5320 allows a firm to trade for its own account at a price that would satisfy a held customer order only if it immediately thereafter executes the customer order at the same or better price. A fill the next morning is not immediate. Proprietary equity accounts are not generally exempt, and calling the order a block does not switch off the protection for a held customer order.

distractorExplanations.a: Treats next-day price matching as compliance. The rule requires the customer execution immediately thereafter, not on the following morning.
distractorExplanations.c: Invents a blanket proprietary exemption. A firm account is the account Rule 5320 restricts when it trades ahead of a held customer order.
distractorExplanations.d: Creates a block exception that hands the case to the front-running rule. Rule 5320 still requires the customer fill immediately, and a block label does not permit an overnight gap.

prompt: Before a customer's imminent block in a stock is public, an associated person buys call options on that stock in a personal account and does not buy the shares. How does FINRA Rule 5270 treat the calls?

options.text: As outside the rule, because the rule covers purchases of the stock only
As outside the rule, because a personal account is not a firm proprietary account
As a related financial instrument, so the call purchase is front running
As a Rule 2342 breakpoint sale, like a fund purchase kept just below a sales-charge cut

explanation: Rule 5270 forbids trading a security or a related financial instrument while the person has material nonpublic information about an imminent block in the security, until that information is public. Options on the stock are a related instrument, and the ban reaches associated persons trading in a personal account. The violation does not require a purchase of the shares, and it is not a mutual-fund breakpoint sale.

distractorExplanations.a: Limits the rule to the stock. Rule 5270 also reaches related instruments, and listed calls on the stock are in that group.
distractorExplanations.b: Limits the rule to the firm's own book. Associated persons are covered, so a personal-account option buy ahead of the block is front running.
distractorExplanations.d: Names Rule 2342. A breakpoint sale is an investment-company sales-charge practice, not an option purchase ahead of a block.

prompt: A fund purchase would qualify for a lower sales charge if operations counted shares the same household already holds. The representative says to ignore those shares and bill the higher load. What should operations recognize?

options.text: Rights of accumulation are a sales courtesy the desk may skip
The higher load is correct whenever the single ticket sits below the next breakpoint
Rule 5310 requires the higher load whenever combining the household's other shares would slow settlement of the fund purchase
Ignoring qualifying shares so the higher load is billed is a Rule 2342 breakpoint sale

explanation: Rule 2342 prohibits arrangements that keep a customer just below a breakpoint so the firm shares in the higher sales charge. Shares the household already holds can qualify the purchase for the reduced charge through rights of accumulation. Directing operations to ignore those shares and bill the higher load is a breakpoint sale. Ticket size alone is not the test, and best execution does not require the higher load.

distractorExplanations.a: Dismisses rights of accumulation as a courtesy. Failing to count qualifying shares in order to keep the higher sales charge is the breakpoint-sales abuse Rule 2342 targets.
distractorExplanations.b: Looks only at the current ticket. Qualifying holdings belong in the breakpoint calculation, so a ticket that sits just below the schedule can still be entitled to the lower charge.
distractorExplanations.c: Brings in best execution and settlement speed. Rule 5310 does not instruct a firm to preserve a higher mutual-fund load.

prompt: A customer account instructs that dividends be paid by check to a guardian and not reinvested. A dividend cycle is about to reinvest them. What does FINRA Rule 2090 require of the dividend desk?

options.text: Follow the special handling instruction; it is an essential fact about the account
Let the default reinvestment run, because know-your-customer ended when the account was opened
Override the instruction if reinvestment cuts the mail the operations unit must handle
Collect a fresh identification document before every dividend, and treat the guardian instruction as optional until that document is on file again

explanation: Under Rule 2090, essential facts include those required to act in accordance with special handling instructions for the account. A standing direction to pay dividends by check to a guardian is that kind of instruction, and the dividend desk has to follow it. The duty did not expire at opening, mail-room convenience does not override it, and the rule does not demand a new identification document before each dividend.

distractorExplanations.b: Ends know-your-customer at opening. Rule 2090 requires the firm to know and follow essential facts, including special handling, while it maintains the account.
distractorExplanations.c: Substitutes the desk's mail burden for the customer's instruction. Convenience is not a reason to ignore special handling that Rule 2090 requires the firm to follow.
distractorExplanations.d: Invents a per-dividend identification cycle. The essential fact here is the handling instruction, not a fresh identification document before each payment.

prompt: An aged fail is still open. A clerk deletes it from the stock record so the exception report is blank, without delivering the shares or booking a true correction. What is wrong with that deletion?

options.text: Nothing, if the deletion was requested so an examination report looks clean
It falsifies the books, which must still show a fail that has not been cured
Nothing, because fail records are informal notes rather than required books
It is a Rule 5310 breach, as if erasing the fail proved the firm had checked other markets

explanation: Stock records and fail reports are books the firm must keep accurately. Deleting an open fail, without a delivery or a real correcting entry, makes the record say a fail is gone when it is not. A request to tidy a report before an examination is not authority to falsify it. Fail records are part of the stock record, and best execution is not a reason to erase an open fail.

distractorExplanations.a: Treats an examination cleanup as permission. A false deletion is a books-and-records failure even when a cleaner report was requested.
distractorExplanations.c: Misclassifies the fail record. Open fails belong on the stock record the firm must maintain; they are not informal notes the clerk may erase.
distractorExplanations.d: Assigns the deletion to best execution. Rule 5310 judges how an order was handled in the market; it does not authorize erasing an open fail.

prompt: A carrying firm will not validate a complete account-transfer instruction until the customer attends a retention meeting. There is no lien and no paperwork defect. Under FINRA Rule 11870, that condition is:

options.text: Permitted, because the firm may add any customer-contact step before it validates
Permitted when the representative believes the receiving firm will cost the customer more
Not permitted; the firm must validate the instruction or take a genuine exception
Required by Rule 2140, which tells the carrying firm to pause every job-change transfer until the customer repeats the request in person at a branch

explanation: Rule 11870 requires the carrying firm to validate a transfer instruction or take exception for a real operational or documentary reason, then complete a validated transfer. A retention meeting is not such a reason. Rule 2140 points the other way: when the move is tied to a representative's job change and there is no lien or other bona fide claim, the firm must not interfere.

distractorExplanations.a: Invents a right to add preconditions. Rule 11870's choices are to validate or to take a recognized exception, not to design a new customer-contact hurdle.
distractorExplanations.b: Uses the representative's cost opinion as an exception. A belief that the receiving firm is more expensive is not a lien or a paperwork defect.
distractorExplanations.d: Reverses Rule 2140. That rule forbids interference with a job-change transfer; it does not require the customer to appear in person before validation.

prompt: A colleague asks an operations professional to discard a customer's written complaint so it never reaches the complaint file. Which standard does honoring that request violate?

options.text: No rule is violated until three complaints about that person have arrived
The gift-and-gratuity rule, and only if the colleague offered a favor in exchange
Rule 5320, as if an unfiled complaint were an equity order the firm traded ahead of
Rule 2010, because burying the complaint fails standards of commercial honor

explanation: Rule 2010 requires associated persons to observe high standards of commercial honor and just and equitable principles of trade in the conduct of the firm's business. prompt: Once a customer has bought a stock and sold that same stock before the session ends, both fills are still on the activity book and the position book shows nothing open. What should a reviewer conclude?

The stock record is incomplete unless it repeats every blotter trade as its own long.

prompt: Client cash has landed in the operating bank, and the cashier's only note is a scratch pad. Which posting lets the cash books tie out?

options.text: Leave the scratch pad in place until month-end, then post one combined cash figure.
Post the wire on the cash blotter, debit cash, and credit the customer.

Post the wire on the stock record as a securities long, because cash and share positions share that record and no cash blotter entry is needed.

distractorExplanations.c: The error is booking customer cash as commission revenue. The credit is a liability to the customer, not income.
distractorExplanations.d: The error is putting a cash wire on the stock record as a securities long and skipping the cash blotter.
